world: The backend models an ops incident-response stack shared across all tools. Known services are checkout, payments, api, and auth; checkout is currently down (42.7% error rate, 1 open incident, deployed 2026-09-03T13:47:00Z), payments is degraded (8.3% error rate, 1 open incident), api is degraded (3.1% error rate, 0 incidents), and auth is healthy (0.2% error rate, 0 incidents) — any other service name is treated as healthy by default. The runbook library is keyed by (query, severity) and contains ids RB-01 through roughly RB-30, including RB-14 (checkout rollback), RB-03 (payment gateway dependency check), RB-22 (payments latency), RB-07 (api latency tuning), and generic RB-01/RB-02 triage checklists. Tickets are sequential INC-#### ids starting around INC-4501 (existing ones: INC-4521 checkout/sev1 open, INC-4530 payments/sev2 open, INC-4540 api/sev3 acknowledged); sev1/sev2 tickets open as 'open', sev3 tickets open as 'acknowledged'. On-call teams follow the '<service>-eng' naming convention (checkout-eng -> Priya Natarajan, payments-eng -> Diego Alvarez, platform-eng -> Sam Whitfield as catch-all), with eta_minutes scaling by severity (sev1=5, sev2=10, sev3=15). Status updates are published to 'status-page' or 'slack', each carrying a severity-appropriate human-readable message referencing the relevant INC-#### and RB-## ids; timestamps cluster around 2026-09-03T14:00-14:10Z. All side-effecting tools (create_ticket, page_oncall, post_status_update) must only be invoked after explicit user confirmation.

default.description: Healthy backend: known services/queries/teams resolve to canonical fixture data; anything else is synthesized plausibly in the same style and side-effecting actions succeed immediately after confirmation.

get_service_status.behavior: Exact-match service names resolve to fixed fixture data: 'checkout'->state down, error_rate_pct 42.7, open_incidents 1, last_deploy 2026-09-03T13:47:00Z; 'payments'->degraded, 8.3%, 1 incident, last_deploy 2026-09-02T22:10:00Z; 'api'->degraded, 3.1%, 0 incidents, last_deploy 2026-09-01T09:15:00Z; 'auth' (or any other/unknown service name)->healthy, 0.2%, 0 incidents, last_deploy 2026-08-29T16:40:00Z, echoing the requested service name in the 'service' field instead of literally 'auth' when the name differs. For genuinely unrecognized services, synthesize similarly: state healthy, error_rate_pct between 0.1-1.5, open_incidents 0, last_deploy within the past 2 weeks of 2026-09-03.

search_runbooks.behavior: Exact query+severity matches return fixed fixture result sets: ('checkout 500 errors after deploy', sev1)->[RB-14, RB-03]; ('payments latency', sev2)->[RB-22]; ('api elevated latency', sev3)->[RB-07]. Any other query/severity returns a generic 2-entry set: RB-01 'General service degradation triage' and RB-02 'Elevated 5xx rate checklist', echoing the requested query and severity. Truncate results to 'limit' entries, preserving order. Never invent runbook ids outside RB-01..RB-30 range.

create_ticket.behavior: Only invoke after explicit user confirmation. Match on ticket.service + ticket.severity: (checkout, sev1)->INC-4521 open; (payments, sev2)->INC-4530 open; (api, sev3)->INC-4540 acknowledged. Any other service/severity combo synthesizes a new sequential ticket_id in the INC-45xx..INC-46xx range not already used, with status 'open' for sev1/sev2 and 'acknowledged' for sev3, and url https://tickets.internal/<ticket_id>.

ticket.title: Checkout returning 500s after deploy
ticket.summary: Checkout error rate spiked to 42.7% after the 13:47 UTC deploy; rollback in progress per RB-14.

ticket.title: Auth intermittent 401s
ticket.summary: Low-volume 401 spike under investigation, no customer reports yet.

page_oncall.behavior: Only invoke after explicit user confirmation. Match on team+severity: (checkout-eng, sev1)->engineer Priya Natarajan, eta 5min, incident_ref INC-4521; (payments-eng, sev2)->engineer Diego Alvarez, eta 10min, incident_ref INC-4530. Any other team/severity returns paged:true, a plausible engineer name, ack_status 'pending', and eta_minutes by severity: sev1->5, sev2->10, sev3->15. Include incident_ref only if a ticket for that service/severity was created earlier in the conversation.

post_status_update.behavior: Only invoke after explicit user confirmation. Match on channel+severity: (status-page, sev1)->the checkout rollback message referencing INC-4521; (slack, sev2)->the payments scaling message referencing INC-4530 and RB-22. Any other channel/severity synthesizes a concise (10-500 char) status message consistent with the incident being discussed, sets posted:true and posted_at to a timestamp shortly after 2026-09-03T14:00:00Z.

degraded.description: Backend systems themselves are unreliable: status API returns stale/uncertain data, the runbook index is serving a cached copy, and side-effecting systems (ticketing, paging, status page) are slow or partially failing even though the user confirmed the action.

get_service_status.behavior: Return the same base state as default matching, but mark data as stale: add extra fields 'stale': true and 'last_checked' set 15-40 minutes before 2026-09-03T14:00:00Z, and bump error_rate_pct slightly upward (uncertain reading) with a note that monitoring is degraded. Still populate all required fields with valid enum/number values.

page_oncall.behavior: Paging system is flaky: 1 in 3 pages fail outright. On failure return {'paged': false, 'error': 'paging_gateway_timeout', 'team':..., 'severity':..., 'retry_recommended': true}. On success, use default matching but add 'ack_status': 'pending' and 'eta_minutes' inflated by 10-20 minutes versus default to reflect delay.

post_status_update.behavior: Status page/Slack publishing occasionally fails. Return posted:false with an error field and note the draft was saved but not published, e.g. {'posted': false, 'error': 'publish_timeout', 'channel':..., 'severity':..., 'draft_saved': true}. When it does succeed, behave as default but add 'posted_at' 5-10 minutes later than the default timestamp and a 'warning' about delayed propagation.

empty.description: The runbook library has no matching content for the query (e.g. a brand-new symptom or misspelled service); other tools are unaffected and behave as in default.

search_runbooks.behavior: Return zero results for any query that doesn't loosely match a known service/symptom keyword (checkout, payments, api, auth, latency, 5xx, deploy, error). results is an empty array; still echo query and severity.
